notes: Scope: the revision commit 8f8d0644 only (census against HEAD~1), plus a narration grep over every field the rulings work changed (census against the merge base with origin/main). The census matches Revision_Round1.json exactly: 14 movement fields (old and new both match), 5 rewritten edges and 1 new edge, no other edge or field touched. node tools/validate-census.mjs: 0 errors, the 2 shortName warnings that were there before. All 28 quotes on the six links match their files at the stated lines (whitespace-normalized; OCR as printed, e.g. 'tlie', 'wliom'). Context reads: HP 7130-7190; Griffith 4425-4445; Langlois 20936-20948, 22686-22698; Ormanian 1868-1876; Glassberger 18520-18592; Bullarium 190-200, 56680-56760, 57020-57035, 79955-80075. Findings R1-01 to R1-13: each fixed as proposed or with a sound departure. R1-02: the Griffith quote widened to 4431-4433 and naming Griffith in the note is right, since the grade is now his reconstruction; Moses III.39 now supports a note sentence on the in-contact link ('the king later put a new head in Nerses's place without the archbishop of Caesarea', 22690-22695, King Bab after Nerses's death). R1-07: 'condemned them to the flames' is closer to Evans/Gibbon (1092-1097) than the proposed 'many were burned', and avoids a number. R1-09: the reviser's departure on 1944 is not sound; see R2-01 (the round 1 fix itself dropped the hedge the ruling 6 draft had rightly applied). R1-14: the new link is sound in type, ID order (l < o), grade and outcome basis. Constance (18553-18555) named Nicholas Rudolphi vicar general over the Observants of the provinces of France, Burgundy and Touraine. In no. 705 (56705-56718) the minister general named Capistrano and Mauberto at the pope's arrangement ('ex Nostra dispositione'); the bull's confirming clause is at 57028-57029. In no. 1007 the pope, 'inhaerentes' to the statutes of Constance and Martin V (80016-80019), 'statuimus, decernimus et ordinamus' (80023-80024) that the chapter elect a vicar general near the end of each three years (80024-80060), and the minister general must confirm him within three days (80063-80066). The outcome is under 30 words (24), ends with a full stop, and the act sits inside its 50-line locus. One gap: see R2-02. Two line ranges are loose but contain their quotes (79991-79997 for a quote at 79990-79993; 80058-80065 for a quote at 80058-80060); not a finding. The disposition of the Open-Gaps closure (passed to Mark, since the reviser edits no repo file) is sound. Prose: every changed field and every changed note and outcome passes score_turn (lowest field FRE 60.8 Paulicians why; highest FK 9.3 the Observant outcome); no sentence passes 25 words (two Alfred sentences at exactly 25). Nothing in the changed prose goes past its source, except R2-01's ruling breach. Margery Kempe (Book I.1-2), Alfred's preface and the 1552 schism are stated within what those texts say; the 1552 relationsSummary drops only 'professes', not an event. Narration grep (we hold|vendored|census|entry|record shows|not checked, plus Library|draft|candidate|counted): no build narration in changed text. Hits are 'appear in the record' (Paulicians) and 'The winning side wrote the record' (iconophiles), both the historical record. 'Not counted as a tradition of its own' (1552 statusDescription) is the field's own status voice, and the revision removed 'candidate tradition' and 'entry' from it.

findings.problem: Brief item 4. 'In 1944 Allied bombing destroyed it' is a guarded fact under ruling 6, not a plain one. The guard is: 'a fact that charges someone with violence or persecution, gives a number, or is disputed needs a source, or is stated as what is reported.' The sentence charges a named party, the Allies, with destroying the abbey, and the Library holds no source for it. The ruling has no exception for an act that its doers admitted or that was recorded. The reviser's reading ('an act admitted and recorded by those who did it, not a charge') adds a test Mark did not rule. The ruling 6 draft rightly classed this fact as guarded ('charges the Lombards, the Saracens and the Allies'). The round 1 fix wrongly dropped the hedge. The same field now gives the Lombards a witness (Paul the Deacon) and the Saracens a witness (the abbey's chronicle). The Allies get none. The earthquake stays plain: it is not violence. The era 3 wants list has Leo of Ostia for 883 but no text for 1944, and the revision's wants add none.

findings.problem: No. 1007 is the bull for the Observants beyond the Alps only (its rule speaks of 'vicarius generalis ipsorum fratrum de observantia ultramontanus', 80024-80025). The note ('the Observants would elect their own vicars general') and the outcome ('the Observants would choose their own leaders') cover both sides of the Alps. Only the editors' note shows the twin bull for the near side, and that note is not among the link's sources. The drafter flagged this. The rule says every fact in an outcome must come from a source already on the link. The text is true; the source for it is missing.
